html:
1Three vision tasks

Task Direction What you use
Interpret an image Image in, text out A multimodal model (vision-enabled) with the image in the prompt
Create an image Text in, image out An image-generation model
Analyze an image with a ready-made service Image in, structured result out Azure Vision image analysis (captions, tags, objects, Read)

2Interpret visual input in a prompt

A vision-enabled multimodal model accepts an image together with text in the same prompt, so you can ask about the picture: "Describe this picture", "What is wrong with this product?", "How many tents are in the photo?".

  • Vision-enabled models include the GPT-5 series, GPT-4.1 series, GPT-4o series and the o-series reasoning models. [Verify live]
  • The message content is a list of parts: a text part and an image part. The image is given as a URL or as base64-encoded data.
  • Image limits exist (size and format, for example about 20 MB and common formats such as JPEG and PNG). [Verify live]

This is the shape of a request from the Microsoft documentation (the older chat completions style):

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=deployment_name,
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this picture:"},
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "<image URL>"}},
        ]},
    ],
    max_tokens=2000,
)
Part Meaning
model=deployment_name The deployment of a vision-enabled model
role: system The assistant's rules (Module 6)
role: user with a list The prompt has several parts
{"type": "text", ...} The question about the image
{"type": "image_url", ...} The image, by URL (or base64 data)
max_tokens The maximum length of the reply
Exam tip

. "The prompt includes an image" → the user message content is a list with a text part and an image part. The model must be vision-enabled. A text-only model rejects or ignores images.

3Create new images with generative models

An image-generation model creates an image from a text prompt.

  • You choose the deployment, the prompt, the number of images, the size and the quality.
  • For gpt-image-1, sizes include 1024×1024, 1024×1536 and 1536×1024; quality can be low, medium or high.
  • The result comes back as base64 image data (no URL), which your app decodes and saves or shows.
  • Model names change quickly: dall-e-3 was retired on March 4, 2026; current GPT-Image models are used instead. [Verify live]
result = client.images.generate(
    model="gpt-image-1",
    prompt="a close-up of a bear walking through the forest",
    n=1,
    size="1024x1024",
    quality="high",
    output_format="png",
)
image_base64 = result.data[0].b64_json
Part Meaning
client.images.generate The image generation call
model="gpt-image-1" The deployment name of the image model
prompt The description of the picture
n=1 How many images
size, quality Dimensions and quality level
result.data[0].b64_json The image as base64 text
Exam tip

. To create a picture use images.generate; to understand a picture use a chat call with an image part. Write clear, specific prompts for images too: subject, style, setting, mood.

Exam tip

. To interpret a picture use a vision-enabled multimodal model; to create a picture use images.generate.

4A vision application with Azure Vision

Azure Vision image analysis returns structured information about an image: caption, tags, objects with bounding boxes, text (Read), people. Use it when you need consistent, labeled results rather than free-form language, or you do not want to deploy a generative model. Newer designs often prefer a multimodal model for open questions. [Verify live]

Need Better fit
"Describe this picture in a sentence and answer follow-up questions" Multimodal model
"Return the list of objects and where they are" Azure Vision object detection
"Read the text on a sign" Azure Vision Read (OCR) or a multimodal model
"Create a poster image from a description" Image-generation model

5Responsible use

Images can contain people and personal data: follow privacy rules (Module 1), tell users when AI-generated images are used (transparency), and check generated images for harmful or biased content.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants customers to upload a photo of a damaged tent and get a written description of the damage. Which kind of model fits?

  • AAn embedding model
  • BA speech synthesis voice
  • CA vision-enabled multimodal model
  • DA reasoning model without vision
Show the answer

Answer: C. A multimodal model with vision can interpret the image sent in the prompt.

S2In a request, how is a question about an image sent to a multimodal chat model?

  • AThe image is sent only as text inside the system prompt
  • BThe user message content is a list with a text part and an image part
  • CThe image is converted to a temperature value first
  • DThe model name contains the image file itself
Show the answer

Answer: B. The user content is a list that mixes text and an image URL or base64 data.

S3A marketing app must create a poster picture from a written description. Which call fits?

  • AA text analysis call on the description
  • Bclient.images.generate with an image model
  • Crecognize_once_async on a recording
  • Dbegin_analyze with prebuilt-invoice
Show the answer

Answer: B. Image generation creates a new image from a text prompt.

S4The image-generation call returns b64_json. What does the app need to do?

  • AUse it as a web address that anyone can open
  • BDecode the base64 data to get the image
  • CSend it to speech synthesis to read it aloud
  • DIgnore it because it is not needed
Show the answer

Answer: B. The image comes back as base64 text that the app decodes and saves or displays.

S5A solution must return the objects in a photo with their positions in a stable format. Which option fits well?

  • AAzure Vision object detection
  • BA system prompt about tone and style
  • CA larger context window for the model
  • DSpeech translation of the audio
Show the answer

Answer: A. Azure Vision object detection returns objects and bounding boxes.

S6Why must the deployed model be "vision-enabled"?

  • AOtherwise it cannot use the temperature setting at all
  • BOtherwise it cannot accept images in the prompt
  • COtherwise it cannot be deployed in the portal at all
  • DOtherwise it cannot use Microsoft Entra ID sign-in
Show the answer

Answer: B. Text-only models cannot interpret image input.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which kind of model interprets an image in a prompt?

Show the answer

A vision-enabled multimodal model.

R2What are the two parts of a user message with an image?

Show the answer

A text part and an image part.

R3Which call creates images?

Show the answer

images.generate.

R4In what form does gpt-image-1 return the image?

Show the answer

Base64 data.

R5Which model was retired on March 4, 2026?

Show the answer

dall-e-3.

R6Which service returns captions, tags and objects?

Show the answer

Azure Vision image analysis.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Interpret vision-enabled multimodal model; user content list: text part + image_url part (URL or base64)
Create images.generate(model, prompt, n, size, quality); result is base64 in data[0].b64_json
Azure Vision caption, tags, objects, Read, people: structured results
Model names change quickly; dall-e-3 retired March 4, 2026
Responsible use privacy, label AI images, check for harm and bias
